channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Trump posta foto ao lado de Flávio e elogia: ‘um jovem inteligente que ama muito o seu país’
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump posted a photo alongside Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) on his Truth Social platform, praising him as 'a young intelligent man who loves his country very much.' The post came on the same day the USTR recommended a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, heightening trade tensions between the two nations.

item.title: Lula faz apelo a Trump para impedir tarifaço: ‘Você me deve uma reunião’
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva directly appealed to Donald Trump to block a proposed 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, stating that Trump 'owes him a meeting' following an agreement made nearly a month ago at the White House for their teams to negotiate within 30 days. Lula said he is awaiting a call from Trump to explain the situation, emphasizing that the tariff announcement did not come from either of them.

item.title: Deputado pede ao STF investigação de Flávio Bolsonaro por suposta influência no tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: Deputy Pastor Henrique Vieira (PSOL-RJ) requested the STF to investigate Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) for allegedly influencing the U.S. tariff increase on Brazilian products following a meeting with Donald Trump. The petition seeks to include Flávio in the same criminal action already probing Eduardo Bolsonaro for coercion, based on suspicions of international articulation to economically pressure Brazil. The PGR is analyzing the request, which cites new facts such as the USTR’s 25% tariff announcement and Flávio’s social media post thanking Trump after the meeting.

item.title: Sob ameaça de 25% de tarifa dos EUA, Brasil tem prazo de mais um mês para negociar
item.description: Brazil has one more month to negotiate with the U.S. amid the threat of a 25% tariff on its exports, according to a preliminary report from the USTR’s Section 301 investigation. The document sets a timeline for consultations, including a public hearing on July 6, with deadlines for participation requests by June 22 and written comments by July 1. The Lula administration has formed a task force led by the finance and development ministers to engage U.S. officials on alleged unfair trade practices, such as favoring local payment systems like PIX and treatment of big tech companies.

item.title: Fim da 6x1: Fecomercio-MG apresenta a presidenciáveis proposta de contratação por hora
item.description: Fecomercio-MG presented the Trabalho/Hora com Direitos Garantidos (THDG) proposal to presidential candidates and legislators, aiming to end the 6x1 work schedule. The model allows hourly hiring with full CLT rights paid in advance, seeks to reduce informality, and offers flexibility for workers such as elderly, women, and youth, while permitting multiple employment links and a 15% bonus over the category's wage floor.

item.title: Rubio exclui Brasil de lista de aliados dos EUA na América Latina
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio praised U.S. friendship with Latin American nations but excluded Brazil, Nicaragua, Cuba, and Venezuela from the list of allies, citing Brazil’s electoral cycle and proposed 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods. President Lula condemned Rubio as 'anti-Latin America' and blamed the Bolsonaro family for U.S. trade threats. Trump affirmed that Iran negotiations are accelerating and said he had a productive talk with Netanyahu, halting announced strikes on Beirut.

item.title: Deputado pede ao STF investigação de Flávio por influenciar tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: Deputy Pastor Henrique Vieira (Psol-RJ) requested that Minister Alexandre de Moraes of the STF investigate Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) for allegedly acting in the United States to influence the imposition of a new tariff against Brazil. The request is based on claims that Flávio is advancing foreign interests that would harm the national economy.

item.title: “Tariflávio” expõe risco de jogar com Trump
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro sought out Donald Trump after the negative impact of the film Dark Horse on his presidential pre-campaign, aiming to recover politically through a photo with the former U.S. president. The strategy mirrored Lula’s approach after the rejection of Jorge Messias to the STF, but analysts warn that aligning with Trump carries significant risks due to international polarization and the controversies surrounding the former American leader.

item.title: Tarcísio critica postura dos EUA em ameaça de novo tarifaço: ‘Isso não faz o menor sentido’
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas criticized the U.S. proposal to impose an additional 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, calling it nonsensical and harmful to the national economy. He argued that the issues under investigation — such as deforestation and ethanol — are not areas where the U.S. sets a standard, and urged the federal government to use diplomacy to negotiate and protect national interests.

item.title: Senado defende imunidade de Vieira em ação movida pela família de Moraes
item.description: The Senate's legal defense argued for parliamentary immunity of Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) in a moral damages lawsuit filed by the wife and children of Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes. The suit stems from Vieira's March SBT News interview where he linked financial flows to the PCC and mentioned the Moraes law firm, which he claims referred only to Banco Master funds received by the firm. The Senate contends the remarks were made in his official capacity as rapporteur of the Organized Crime CPI and are thus protected by parliamentary immunity.

item.title: PT fala em 'Tariflávio', enquanto oposição tenta se desassociar de tarifas de Trump
item.description: Following the U.S. announcement of a 25% tariff on Brazilian imports, PT supporters on social media linked the decision to Flávio Bolsonaro’s visit to the White House, coining the term 'Tariflávio' as a subtle critique. The opposition sought to distance itself from Trump’s tariffs, claiming the move is unilateral and not tied to any Brazilian candidate’s stance.

item.title: Ameaças ao Pix e de novo tarifaço expõem Flávio e podem dar vitória a Lula em eleição apertada, dizem analistas
item.description: Donald Trump's threats to the Pix payment system and proposed 25% tariffs on Brazilian products may electorally benefit Lula by reinforcing his national sovereignty narrative, while harming Flávio Bolsonaro due to his ties with the American right. Analysts argue this political effect could outweigh the negative economic impacts of U.S. measures and prove decisive in a tight election. Furthermore, Flávio's weakening could create opportunities for alternative right-wing candidates like Ronaldo Caiado, who are better positioned to exploit divisions within the conservative camp.

item.title: Ao vivo: Flávio recebe título de cidadão honorário na Câmara de BH
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro received the honorary citizenship title at the Belo Horizonte Municipal Council on Tuesday, June 2, 2026, proposed by Liberal Party councilors led by councilor Vile Santos. The honor aims to recognize his trajectory and welcome him as a pre-candidate for the Presidency of the Republic. This marks Flávio Bolsonaro's first visit to the Minas Gerais state capital during the 2026 pre-campaign period.

item.title: Crusoé: Aécio sobre Joesley: “É o verdadeiro filho do Lula”
item.description: Federal deputy and PSDB president Aécio Neves criticized businessman Joesley Batista on Papo Antagonista, calling him 'the true son of Lula'. The criticism followed the 2017 audio leak in which Joesley provided the Prosecutor’s Office with a recording showing Aécio and Batista agreeing to a R$2 million loan to pay defense lawyers. Aécio implied that Joesley acts in alignment with Lula’s interests, suggesting petista influence or complicity.

item.title: Deputado pede inclusão de Flávio em inquérito após proposta de tarifa dos EUA
item.description: Federal Deputy Pastor Henrique Vieira (Psol-RJ) filed a formal complaint with the STF requesting that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) be included as an investigated party in the inquiry that already made former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro a defendant for coercion. The request is based on the U.S. tariff proposal on Brazilian goods, which Vieira alleges was orchestrated to pressure the Brazilian government and constitutes an act of coercion involving Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Marco Rubio coloca Brasil fora do grupo ‘países amigáveis’ aos EUA e cita eleições nacionais
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Brazil is not part of the group of countries considered aligned with Washington's interests in Latin America, listing it as an exception alongside Cuba, Nicaragua, and Venezuela. He noted that Brazil is currently in the midst of an electoral cycle, which may justify its temporary exclusion from the coalition of friendly nations. The remarks come amid rising trade tensions, including a proposed 25% tariff on Brazilian goods by the USTR and the U.S. designation of Brazilian criminal factions as foreign terrorist organizations.

item.title: Lula diz que EUA anunciaram, de forma intempestiva, taxação em 25% com base em uma mentira
item.description: President Lula accused the U.S. of imposing a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods based on a 'lie', noting the U.S. has held a $415 billion trade surplus with Brazil over the last 15 years. He linked the move to American concerns over Brazil’s Pix payment system, which he said threatens U.S. credit card companies, and called for a call with Trump to resolve the dispute, insisting Brazil will not be treated as a 'banana republic'.

item.title: Trump não tem candidato nas eleições brasileiras, só interesses
item.description: Donald Trump does not endorse any specific candidate in Brazil's 2026 elections but acts according to U.S. strategic interests. His administration designated PCC and CV as terrorist organizations following Flávio Bolsonaro's visit to Washington, boosting opposition rhetoric, while imposing 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods to support Lula's narrative of threatened sovereignty. Both candidates deny influencing U.S. decisions, which are driven solely by American interests.

item.title: Caiado promete derrotar o PT e classificar facções como terroristas
item.description: Former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) promised to defeat the PT and classify criminal factions as terrorists if elected president in 2026, during a speech at the Megaleite opening in Minas Gerais. He linked the rise of organized crime to federal government actions and advocated for tougher measures against criminal groups.

item.title: Zema satiriza “Gilmarpalooza” e degustação de Macallan
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) satirized the 2026 Lisbon Forum in the 7th episode of 'The Untouchables', using AI-generated puppets to criticize luxury and corporate sponsorships in judiciary events, including Macallan whisky tastings and Banco Master sponsorship, while referencing a real 2024 meeting between Alexandre de Moraes and Vorcaro. The video also ironyically links sponsorships to individuals investigated by the STF, employing 'brain rot' memes like 'six seven'.

item.title: Chanceler de Lula estará em mesmo evento que representante comercial de Trump
item.description: Brazil's Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer will attend the same OECD event in Paris, where Greer is expected to defend proposed 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods, citing unfair trade practices. The Lula government claims the investigation originated from political ties to the Bolsonaro family and is working through diplomatic channels to prevent the tariffs from being implemented. The USTR's inclusion of Brazil's Pix payment system in the investigation has also been criticized by Brasília as baseless.

item.title: Trump posta foto com Flávio depois de anunciar tarifa ao Brasil
item.description: President Donald Trump posted a photo with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) one day after announcing a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, following a White House meeting where they discussed designating Brazilian criminal factions as terrorist organizations. Flávio urged Trump to avoid the tariffs, citing a future cooperative Brazilian government, while the U.S. denied his influence on the PCC and CV designation.

item.title: Cabo eleitoral ou algoz? EUA entram em definitivo na cena eleitoral brasileira
item.description: The U.S. has intensified its influence on Brazil's presidential race with mixed signals: Trump courted the Bolsonaro-led opposition while expressing admiration for Lula, ultimately advancing an America First agenda. Proposals to designate Brazilian criminal groups as terrorists and impose a 25% tariff on Brazilian exports are poised to affect both the economy and the electoral landscape, particularly tying Flávio Bolsonaro to perceptions of subservience to Washington. The government views the situation as advantageous, using it to bolster sovereignty narratives, while Lula’s camp sees it as a 'silver bullet' to galvanize support.

item.title: Trump publica foto com o “esperto jovem” Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump posted two photos on Truth Social alongside Flávio Bolsonaro, praising him as a 'smart young man' who loves Brazil. The meeting took place in the Oval Office at the White House. The post was published on Tuesday, April 2, 2025.

item.title: Com faixa em defesa do Pix, Lula diz que novo tarifaço de Trump foi basado numa 'mentira': 'Estou esperando telefonema dele'
item.description: President Lula claimed the proposed 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods were based on a 'lie', arguing the real U.S. concern is Pix's impact on American credit card companies. He also criticized the Bolsonaro family, linking Flávio and Eduardo Bolsonaro to the U.S. proposal and calling them 'traitors' for seeking foreign interference in Brazilian elections. Lula said he is waiting for a call from Trump to clarify the breakdown of the 30-day negotiation agreement made in May.

item.title: Governistas reagem à proposta de tarifa de Trump e defendem o Pix
item.description: Government allies reacted to the U.S. proposal for a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, defending the Pix payment system as a national achievement and criticizing the Bolsonaro family for alleged influence on the U.S. trade investigation. Deputies such as Gleisi Hoffmann, Erika Hilton, and Lindbergh Farias stated Brazil will not concede on Pix and will pursue diplomatic solutions.

item.title: Trump faz Pix eleitoral e entrega bandeira da liberdade de pagamento a Lula
item.description: The Trump administration symbolically handed Lula a flag related to payment freedom via Pix, using it as a tool to strengthen Brazil’s political narrative on trade disputes with the U.S. Although the issue involves customs tariffs and free competition — topics typically unengaging for the general public — the strategy aims to make the subject more accessible and viral in Brazil’s electoral context. The move reflects an effort to leverage trade tensions for domestic political gain in both countries.

item.title: Quais são os feriados de junho e qual o mais importante que terá alcance nacional?
item.description: June 2026 has no national holidays by federal law, but Corpus Christi, observed on June 11, is expected to create one of the year's longest holiday periods, especially when combined with weekends, affecting millions of Brazilians through travel, June festivities, and changes in business operations.

item.title: Flávio volta ao Nordeste em ida à Bahia que pode emparedar ACM por apoio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign plans a visit to Bahia on April 9 to strengthen Northeastern support and pressure ACM Neto into publicly declaring his backing for the Bolsonaro candidacy. The trip follows earlier events in Rio Grande do Norte and Paraíba in March and aims to place ACM Neto in an awkward position, as he avoids openly aligning with Flávio despite PL party support. ACM Neto's endorsement is considered crucial for Bolsonaro's success in Bahia.

item.title: ‘Uberização’, big techs, caso Mari Ferrer: veja o que o STF julga este mês
item.description: The STF will rule in June on issues including the 'uberization' of labor and digital platform liability for third-party content, the validity of evidence obtained through victim coercion in rape cases, and rules on mining in Indigenous lands. The Court will also decide on the continuation of FPE distribution rules after a temporary extension by Minister Cármen Lúcia, as well as on special retirement for unhealthy working conditions, tax exemptions for persons with disabilities buying vehicles, and the sharing of tax data with the Electoral Public Prosecutor's Office in investigations of illegal campaign donations.

item.title: Choque entre van e caminhão mata cinco estudantes de colégio militar em Goiás
item.description: Five students aged 11 to 14 from the State Military Police College died and eleven others were injured in a crash between a van and a stationary truck on GO-518 in Córrego do Ouro, Goiás. Governor Daniel Vilela, former governor Ronaldo Caiado, and pre-candidate Marconi Perillo expressed sorrow over the tragedy, which led to official mourning and school suspensions in the area.

item.title: Lula diz que 'filhos são piores que Bolsonaro' ao associar taxação dos EUA à família do ex-presidente: 'Traidores da pátria'
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) claimed that the sons of former President Jair Bolsonaro (PL) are 'worse than him', linking them to the U.S. proposal to impose a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, which he labeled as 'traitors of the homeland'. Lula specifically criticized Flávio Bolsonaro for allegedly thanking Donald Trump for the measure, arguing it would harm Brazilian agribusiness and entrepreneurs. The tariff is not yet in effect, awaiting the conclusion of the formal U.S. investigation and required public consultations.

item.title: Flávio espera Cleitinho em MG e diz que não acredita em aliança Zema-Caiado
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) expressed hope of running alongside Cleitinho Azevedo (Republicanos) in Minas Gerais, regardless of the office Cleitinho seeks, and dismissed the likelihood of a joint Romeu Zema (Novo) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) presidential ticket, saying he does not believe they will unite in a standalone candidacy. He emphasized his goal of uniting forces to remove the PT from government, citing recent meetings with Zema at agribusiness events.

item.title: Regulação das big techs na mira dos debates do ‘Gilmarpalooza’
item.description: At the Lisbon Forum, nicknamed 'Gilmarpalooza', Ministers Gilmar Mendes and Alexandre de Moraes advocated for the regulation of big techs, arguing that unregulated algorithms threaten democracy and electoral integrity. They emphasized that the lack of digital rules undermines democratic will formation and that the Judiciary acts as a guarantor of institutional stability, despite criticism of overreach. The expectation for the 2026 elections, with Nunes Marques as TSE president, is a contest with less judicial intervention, given his appointment by Bolsonaro.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula entrega hospital da Universidade Federal de Catalão
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva participates in the delivery ceremony of the university hospital at the Federal University of Catalão, in Goiás, on Tuesday, June 2, 2026. The facility, covering 12,600 m², received investments from the Ministry of Health for equipment including CT scanners, X-ray machines, electric beds, and ICU and surgical center tools. Health Minister Alexandre Padilha also attends the event.

item.title: Governo Lula não pretende rebater EUA sobre novas tarifas
item.description: The Lula government does not intend to point-by-point rebut the new 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian products, arguing that criticisms were already addressed in a prior letter and that the move has political motivation. A political note will be published on Tuesday (June 2, 2026), while Lula is in Goiás and ministries hold emergency meetings to discuss the response. Brazil’s strategy focuses on the bilateral working group established in May, with a deadline for progress by July 15.

item.title: Embaixador indicado pelos EUA eleva tensão de Lula com Trump e dá gás à direita brasileira
item.description: The appointment of Daniel Perez, a Florida Republican and Trump ally, as U.S. ambassador to Brazil heightens tensions between Lula and Trump, especially following the U.S. designation of PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist groups and the imposition of 25% tariffs on Brazilian imports, which bolsters the Bolsonaro narrative in Brazil's 2026 presidential race.

item.title: Planalto vê situação adversa e prevê cenário similar ao de 2025 em caso de novas tarifas dos EUA
item.description: The Lula government assesses that a potential 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian exports would create a strong domestic political impact, recreating an adverse scenario similar to the July 2025 tariff shock. The Planalto Palace maintains the order to negotiate until July, avoiding conflicting rhetoric and opting for a technical and diplomatic response, as done previously. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) made a preventive statement urging Trump not to tax Brazilian companies, fearing electoral backlash due to the contradiction with the Bolsonaro family’s past support for U.S. tariffs.

item.title: Flávio fala em “perseguição” após operação contra produtora de “Dark Horse”
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) criticized the São Paulo Civil Police operation against the producer of the film 'Dark Horse', suggesting it may be a state persecution aimed at influencing the 2026 elections. He defended Ricardo Nunes' administration and called the film's financing a 'smokescreen' to divert attention from federal issues, such as Correios' losses. The investigation examines whether R$ 108 million in public funds meant for community Wi-Fi was diverted to finance the biopic on Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Zema diz que não tem rabo preso: “De idiotas só quero vaias”
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and pre-candidate for the presidency in 2026 from the Novo party, stated he has 'nothing to hide' and will continue denouncing irregularities in the country, citing suspicious contracts involving allies of Minister Gilmar Mendes and reaffirming his commitment to transparency. He highlighted that his administration in Minas Gerais was well evaluated and restored the state's finances, reinforcing his confidence in the pre-campaign.

item.title: Trump é um parceiro incômodo tanto para o petismo quanto para o bolsonarismo
item.description: Recent actions by Donald Trump, including the threat of 25% tariffs on Brazilian exports and support for labeling Brazilian criminal factions as terrorist organizations, are creating political repercussions in Brazil. While Bolsonarism is criticized for its servile stance toward the U.S., the Lula government faces backlash for failing to negotiate effectively with Washington, despite personal rapport signals. The dynamic reveals a toxic and unpredictable relationship with Trump that politically benefits figures like Flávio Bolsonaro but undermines national sovereignty and fuels internal instability.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro tenta se desvincular de possível novo tarifaço
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) stated he urged President Donald Trump and U.S. officials not to impose tariffs on Brazilian companies, a week after his White House visit where he emphasized his close ties with the Republican. His remarks represent a shift in rhetoric, moving from promoting his privileged relationship with Washington to defending national interests amid the threat of new U.S. tariffs. He also suggested the Lula administration use the public consultation period to negotiate and avoid trade sanctions.

item.title: Equipe de Lula questiona por que Flávio Bolsonaro não revelou antes ter defendido empresas brasileiras
item.description: Lula’s team questions why Flávio Bolsonaro did not disclose during his meeting with Trump that he had requested the U.S. not to tax Brazilian companies, noting he had only publicized his request to label PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations. Presidential aides doubt the truth of his recent claim and accuse him of sabotaging ongoing trade negotiations with the U.S., threatening to hold him accountable if the proposed 25% tariffs on Brazilian imports are implemented starting July 15.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro reage após ameaça de novas tarifas do governo Trump: 'Pedi para não taxar nossas empresas'
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, a pre-candidate for president, criticized the Trump administration's threat of 25% retaliatory tariffs on Brazilian goods, stating he had directly urged Trump not to tax Brazilian companies. He advocated for serious negotiations over tariffs, accusing Lula of acting with bravado. The proposed U.S. measures are under public consultation until July 1, with a public hearing scheduled for July 6.

item.title: Causos judiciais
item.description: The text reflects on the rich literary production of Brazilian judges and magistrates, highlighting figures such as Paulo Bomfim and Vladimir Passos de Freitas, who transformed their judicial experiences into works of poetry, essays, and memory. It laments the loss of many informal court narratives that could have formed a unique library of humor, sensitivity, and judicial history. The mention of Edmeu Calmesini's book serves as a trigger for this reflection on judicial folklore and the importance of preserving these narratives.

item.title: Quem é e o que pensa o deputado da Flórida escolhido por Trump para ser embaixador dos EUA no Brasil
item.description: Florida state representative Daniel Perez, a Cuban-American ally of Donald Trump, has been nominated by the president to serve as U.S. ambassador to Brazil. The appointment awaits Senate approval. Perez emphasizes his work on child welfare, health, education, and electoral integrity, while publicly supporting Trump, the MAGA movement, and actions such as the capture of Nicolás Maduro.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula inaugura o Campus Catalão do IF Goiano
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva inaugurated the permanent campus of IF Goiano in Catalão, southeast Goiás, with R$6.5 million from the Novo PAC, covering over 70% of the total investment. The campus has 1,210 enrollments and offers professional qualification courses. Later, Lula attended the inauguration of the UFCAT University Hospital, serving 56 municipalities in the Central-Southeast macro-region of Goiás, which received R$27 million from the Ministry of Health for equipment.

item.title: O que é Seção 301? Entenda lei dos EUA que permite novo tarifaço de 25% contra o Brasil
item.description: The U.S. Trade Representative completed a Section 301 investigation and proposed a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, with exemptions for coffee, meat, aircraft and other items listed in a 73-page exception list. The measure, based on allegations of unreasonable and burdensome Brazilian practices, was initiated in July 2025 by Donald Trump and must be finalized by July 2026. Despite ongoing bilateral talks, no sufficient progress was made to avert the tariff proposal.

item.title: EUA citam prática comercial desleal e propõem tarifa de 25% ao Brasil
item.description: The U.S. has proposed a 25% tariff on Brazilian imports, citing unfair trade practices such as weak intellectual property protection, corruption, ethanol market access, and inadequate environmental enforcement. The move, grounded in Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act, follows a May meeting between Lula and Trump and gives Brazil until July 15 to respond. Exemptions include beef, coffee, rare earth metals, aircraft equipment, and some fruits and vegetables.

item.title: Café, carnes, aeronaves e mais: os itens brasileiros poupados do novo tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: The U.S. proposed a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods but issued a 73-page list of exemptions preserving key exports such as coffee, meats, fruits, cereals, minerals, rare earths, Brazilian aircraft and aerospace parts, plus organic chemicals, pharmaceuticals and fertilizers. The measure stems from a Section 301 trade investigation launched in July 2025 under President Trump, with a deadline for implementation set for July 2026. While the USTR criticized Brazil in areas like digital trade, deforestation and intellectual property, it acknowledged constructive engagement by the Brazilian government and noted ongoing bilateral talks to avoid further trade barriers.
